correctness.rationale: The arbitrary-diameter-two graph tail follows by categorizing same-edge, incident-edge and disjoint-edge pairs; an edge pair with a cross-adjacency has distance at most 5/2, while an induced 2K2 pair has distance exactly 2 plus two independent Uniform[0,1/2] distances to its nearest endpoints. The coefficient 4M_2/m^2 follows. For the fixed Shrikhande and rook graphs, verify.py enumerates all 1128 unordered edge pairs of each explicit 48-edge graph, verifies diameter and strongly regular parameters, and evaluates exact rational clipping areas at all 18 spline interpolation controls. Polygon clipping configurations change only at half-integer radii, making three controls per interval conclusive for each quadratic branch. The resulting full difference is a squared tent of height 1/96, with diagnostic CDFs 11/12 and 29/32.

value.rationale: The classical nonisomorphic cospectral strongly regular pair is a canonical reconstruction challenge. A complete exact comparison of intrinsically sampled metric-edge distance laws, including an interval of provable blindness and a sharp discriminating squared tent, is a natural structural invariant. The universal diameter-two tail simultaneously reconstructs induced 2K2 counts from one measurable radius, extending significance beyond an ad hoc finite table. The finite exact fraction 1/96 is motivated by that graph comparison, not an arbitrary parameter choice.
